chunks: 1181 - Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated from him that he said:

A resident should not lead a traveler, nor should a traveler lead a resident. If a man is tried with something of that and leads a group of residents, then when he completes the two rakʿahs, he should give salām, then take one of them by the hand and put him forward, and he should lead them. And when the traveler prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer as two rakʿahs and give salām.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer to be completed by the traveler
key_terms.الْحَضَرِيُّ: a resident, meaning one who is not traveling
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: a traveler whose prayer is shortened
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, meaning praying in congregation behind an Imam
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: he gave the taslim ending the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat in this specific legal context
key_terms.فَقَدَّمَهُ: he placed him forward to lead the remainder
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads in congregational salat as Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a traveler and a resident leading each other in congregational salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning congregational salat involving a resident and a traveler. It explains how the prayer should be managed when such a situation occurs, especially regarding completing two rakʿahs and handing over leadership when needed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1181 - Dawud ibn Al-Hussain narrated that the Imam (as) said:

"A resident (non-traveler) should not lead a traveler, nor should a traveler lead a resident. If a man finds himself in a situation where he must lead a congregation of residents and completes two rak'ahs, he should then offer the taslim (salutation of peace), take the hand of one of the residents, and place him to lead the rest. When a traveler prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer with two rak'ahs and then offer the taslim."
